title: ArcGIS-based protocol to calculate area fraction of landslide for catchments
author: Yoshihara

steps.title: Prepare Required Data and Software
steps.instruction: Ensure access to ArcGIS software with an advanced license and prepare the necessary input data.

substeps.instruction: Obtain surface raster data of digital elevation.
Obtain a shapefile of landslide polygons.

steps.title: Execute Initial Model Processing
steps.instruction: Run Model 1 using the ArcGIS ModelBuilder utility to generate the flow accumulation raster.

steps.title: Visualize Streamlines
steps.instruction: Configure the flow accumulation raster symbology in the ArcGIS map window to visualize the streamline.

substeps.instruction: Add the flow accumulation raster to the map window.
Set the number of classes to '2'.
Set the symbol for values less than 1000 to no color (transparent).
Set the symbol for values 1000 and above to a color of the operator's preference (e.g., blue).

steps.title: Determine Catchment Outlets
steps.instruction: Create a shapefile containing points that represent the outlets of the study catchments.

substeps.instruction: Place catchment outlet points precisely on the visualized streamline of the flow accumulation raster to ensure successful watershed raster creation in Model 2.

steps.title: Calculate Area Fractions
steps.instruction: Use the remaining ArcGIS ModelBuilder models to calculate the catchment area (CA), landslide area (LA), and landslide scar area percentage (LCR).

substeps.instruction: Run Model 2 to create the watershed raster using the outlet points.
Calculate LCR using the formula: (LA / CA) × 100.

description: This method was designed to calculate the percentage of landslide area (LA)/catchment area (CA) for 37 forested catchments in Hokkaido, Japan, where shallow landslides (i.e., destabilization of soil-mantled hillslope) occurred due to the Hokkaido Eastern Iburi earthquake in 2018 (6.6 Mw). However, this method can also be used to obtain the area fraction of surface information other than LAs (e.g., specific kinds of land use or lithology) within catchments. The method requires an operator to use the ArcGIS software with an advanced license and prepare surface raster data of digital elevation and a shapefile of landslide polygons. The procedure consists of six models based on the ModelBuilder utility in ArcGIS. The resulting output visualizes catchment outlines and landslide distribution within the study catchments and calculates the CA, LA, and area percentage of landslide scar (LCR) described as LA/CA × 100. The presented method was applied to forested catchments in southern Hokkaido, Japan [1]. In this region, more than 6000 shallow landslides were caused by the Hokkaido Eastern Iburi earthquake in 2018 [2,3]. The distribution of the shallow landslides was manually defined by referring to DEMs and aerial photographs before and after the earthquake. Fig. 7a shows a result of the application of our suggested method [1]. In this case, 37 catchments were analyzed and the CA, LA, and LCR were in the range of 0.08–2.56 km2, 0–0.70 km2, and 0–66%, respectively. Editing outlet points were performed to generate a different result (Fig. 7b). In this case, three outlets of the catchment were set and the CA, LA, and LCR were in the range of 8.52–11.47 km2, 0.71–3.91 km2, and 8–34%, respectively.Fig. 7Validation results of the method used in forested catchments in Hokkaido, Japan, where shallow landslides were caused by the Hokkaido Eastern Iburi earthquake in 2018.
